audit.why: 51.87% Emerald+ for Kassadin, EVEN at 5.5/10. Rumble owns levels 1-2 on Flamespitter chip, the lane levels out at 3-5 once Nether Blade and Force Pulse exist, and Kassadin owns everything from 6. That is exactly the shape the mirrored Rumble audit (audits/top/rumble__kassadin.json) settled on, so both directions now say the same thing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart said Rumble at Level 3, Levels 4-5, First item and Two+ items — four stages he does not win, and four captions that say so. whys[2] ends 'call it even', whys[3] calls it 'a standoff', whys[5] says 'tilt the lane your way', whys[6] says 'his AP flatlines while yours peaks'. The mirrored Rumble page states the same split from his side.
audit.why: Rumble's power is front-loaded on Flamespitter and The Equalizer; he has no scaling answer to a maxed Riftwalk, and the content layer already says he is the rare AP who does not out-scale Kassadin.
audit.corrected: Level 3 and Levels 4-5 to Skill; Level 6, First item and Two+ items to Kassadin, on win[] and phases[].side. This matches the mirror exactly — Rumble owns 1-2, even at 3-5, Kassadin from 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single biggest interaction in this lane was absent from both layers: Rumble's Overheat. Riot's Junkyard Titan text says that at 100% Heat 'he starts Overheating, gaining bonus Attack Speed and granting his basic attacks bonus damage, but making him unable to cast spells for a few seconds.' Instead the full layer names Scrap Shield as the matchup-defining ability and builds every green light around it, and the content layer misuses 'overheated' to mean the Danger Zone empowerment ('his overheated Flamespitter ticks', 'Overheat his autos and Flamespitter to bully you') — which inverts the mechanic, because while Overheating he cannot cast Flamespitter at all. Separately, breakdown.late claims a 'Q-silence' Kassadin does not have.
audit.why: Danger Zone is 50% Heat and empowers his basic abilities; Overheating is 100% Heat and locks them out. Those are opposite states and the page used one word for both.
audit.corrected: Heat is now the tracked bar instead of Scrap Shield: Danger Zone is named as the empowered state, and the 100% Overheat lockout is named as the all-in window, with the honest caveat that his autos hit harder during it. The silence claim is replaced with the interrupt.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d told you Rumble burning Scrap Shield is a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is 6 seconds flat. A fifteen-second window does not exist, and waiting for a 6s shield is not a plan.
audit.corrected: Scrap Shield is stated as 6s and demoted; the real windows given are the Overheat lockout and the Electro Harpoon slow being spent. Flamespitter's 10s rank-1 cooldown is added too.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere said that Electro Harpoon reduces your Magic Resist.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'slowing their Move Speed, and reducing their Magic Resist.' Against an all-magic opponent the obvious defensive buy is MR, and his E actively undoes it — which is precisely why Void Stone's flat percentage reduction and raw HP from Rod of Ages are the mitigation that survives contact.

edits.before: Rumble owns these levels. His Flamespitter is sustained AP DPS that out-trades your single Null Sphere, and if he lands Electro Harpoon to slow you he plants the flame under your feet so you can't simply walk out of the burn. Don't trade back into a melee disadvantage with no Nether Blade mana sustain or Force Pulse pressure yet — last-hit at max Q range and accept the chip. Your saving grace is Void Stone: Flamespitter is entirely magic damage, so your innate 15% magic reduction softens every tick he overheats onto you.
edits.after: Rumble owns these levels. Flamespitter is sustained magic DPS that out-trades your single Null Sphere, and if Electro Harpoon slows you he plants the cone under your feet so you cannot walk out of the burn. Don't trade back into a melee disadvantage with no Nether Blade mana or Force Pulse yet — last-hit at max Q range and accept the chip. Two things save you: Void Stone's flat 15% magic reduction taxes every tick of his all-magic kit, and at 100% Heat he Overheats and cannot cast a spell for a few seconds. That lockout is the window you walk into.

edits.before: Once Nether Blade is restoring your mana off W-empowered autos and Force Pulse is online, you stabilize toward even — farm under tower and use Null Sphere's 1.5s shield to blank a chunk of his overheated burst. The lane truly flips at 6: Riftwalk lets you blink out of The Equalizer carpet or straight onto Rumble the moment his Electro Harpoon slow is down. Bait the Harpoon, blink the instant it's on cooldown, and Q-shield through the Flamespitter he left burning where you used to stand.
edits.after: Once Nether Blade is restoring your mana off W-empowered autos and Force Pulse is online, you stabilize toward even — farm under tower and use Null Sphere's shield to blank a chunk of his Danger Zone burst. The lane truly flips at 6: Riftwalk lets you blink out of The Equalizer carpet or onto Rumble the moment his Electro Harpoon slow is down. Better still, read his Heat bar — at 100% he Overheats and cannot cast at all for a few seconds, and no 6-second Scrap Shield answers an all-in inside that window.

edits.before: This is the matchup you scale for. With Rod of Ages stalled into Nashor's or Lich Bane and Riftwalk maxed, your blink-spam mobility plus Void Stone's magic reduction make Rumble's whole AP kit feel sluggish — you weave through The Equalizer and burst him down before Scrap Shield and its move speed can save him. He's the rare AP that doesn't out-scale you, so unlike a Vladimir or Cassiopeia lane the 2+ items window is yours outright. Just respect a well-placed Equalizer flank in teamfights and Riftwalk out of the zone rather than through it.
edits.after: This is the matchup you scale for. With Rod of Ages stalled into Nashor's or Lich Bane and Riftwalk maxed, your blink-spam plus Void Stone's magic reduction make Rumble's whole AP kit feel sluggish — you weave through The Equalizer and burst him before Scrap Shield's 6-second speed can save him. He's the rare AP that doesn't out-scale you, so unlike a Vladimir or Cassiopeia lane the 2+ items window is yours outright. One buying note: Electro Harpoon shreds your magic resist, so flat MR pays less here than HP plus Void Stone's percentage. Riftwalk out of an Equalizer flank, never through it.

notes: Mirror reuse: audits/top/rumble__kassadin.json was already written, and I took its settled facts rather than re-deriving them — Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s (so no cooldown to wait out; mana is the brake), Void Stone is permanent magic reduction and not a shield, Null Sphere carries the shield on cast, and Kassadin has no silence. The stage split now matches the mirror exactly: Rumble 1-2, even 3-5, Kassadin 6 onward. False positive to ignore: _missing-interactions.json has 'Rumble can deny your mobility (Riftwalk (R)) with Scrap Shield (W), The Equalizer (R)'. Neither ability grounds — Scrap Shield is a shield plus move speed and The Equalizer is a damaging flame wall; the row comes from stray terrain/knockup flags on rumble.json. Nothing in Rumble's kit stops Riftwalk, and I did not write that claim.
